content.value_statement: Complex defects waste time when investigation relies on guesswork. This skill applies reproducible experiments, targeted instrumentation, profiling, and verification to identify root causes.
actual_capabilities: Structures investigations around reproduction, evidence gathering, testable hypotheses, controlled experiments, and fix verification.
Guides regression isolation with binary search, Git history comparison, and git bisect.
Suggests targeted logging, tracing, assertions, breakpoints, heap snapshots, and CPU profiling.
Provides debugging examples for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go.
Helps compare working and failing environments, data, users, versions, and configurations.
Creates focused checklists for intermittent bugs, performance problems, and production incidents.
limitations: The skill cannot access applications, logs, traces, debuggers, or runtime environments by itself.
Useful diagnosis requires an observable symptom and enough evidence to form testable hypotheses.
Code samples are illustrative and require adaptation to the project language, framework, and safety controls.
Production investigation still requires access approval, privacy safeguards, rollback planning, and environment-specific testing.

use_cases.title: Isolate an Application Defect
use_cases.description: Turn an error report into reproduction steps, ranked hypotheses, controlled tests, and clear verification criteria.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Production Incident
use_cases.description: Compare logs, traces, metrics, deployments, and environments while keeping production changes controlled.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Performance Regression
use_cases.description: Select profiling tools, measure bottlenecks, compare versions, and confirm improvement with repeatable benchmarks.

prompt_templates.title: Triage an Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me debug [error]. Ask for missing reproduction details, then create a short plan to isolate the cause and verify the fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner investigation of a reproducible application error

prompt_templates.title: Isolate a Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this regression: [symptom], last working version [version], current version [version], and recent changes [changes]. Propose a git bisect plan with pass criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate investigation after a recent code or dependency change

prompt_templates.title: Profile a Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose [slow operation] using these measurements: [metrics]. Rank likely bottlenecks, choose profiling evidence, and define before-and-after benchmarks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance diagnosis with available runtime measurements

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Distributed Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this distributed incident using [logs], [traces], [metrics], and [deployment timeline]. Rank hypotheses, define controlled tests, and include rollback and verification criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production analysis across services and runtime signals

output_examples.input: Checkout requests fail after deployment, but only for large orders.
output: Leading hypothesis: the deployment changed validation or resource limits for large payloads.
Compare order sizes, deployment differences, request limits, and logs from working and failing requests.
Run one controlled boundary test, apply the fix in staging, and repeat the original reproduction.

output_examples.input: An API became slower after a dependency update.
output: Establish latency and resource baselines for both dependency versions.
Profile database calls, synchronous input and output, allocation pressure, and external service timing.
Confirm the cause by changing one variable and repeating the same benchmark.

output_examples.input: A service fails intermittently during peak traffic.
output: Correlate failures with load, timing, state transitions, deployments, and dependency health.
Prioritize race conditions, resource exhaustion, timeouts, and out-of-order asynchronous work.
Add focused tracing and stress tests, then verify recovery and recurrence behavior.

best_practices: Reproduce the symptom and record the exact environment, inputs, errors, and recent changes before proposing a fix.
Change one variable per experiment and define evidence that would confirm or reject each hypothesis.
Verify the root-cause fix with the original reproduction, regression tests, and relevant performance measurements.
anti_patterns: Do not make several speculative changes at once because the result will not identify the responsible variable.
Do not expose secrets, personal data, or production records in logs, traces, prompts, or test fixtures.
Do not test disruptive hypotheses directly in production without authorization, safeguards, monitoring, and rollback criteria.

faq.question: Which programming languages does this skill support?
faq.answer: The playbook includes JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go examples. Its investigation process also applies to other languages.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands or modify my project?
faq.answer: No. It provides investigation guidance and examples. You decide which tools, commands, and changes are appropriate.

faq.question: Can I use it during a production incident?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide sanitized logs, traces, metrics, and deployment context. Follow your access, privacy, change-control, and rollback procedures.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the observed behavior, expected behavior, reproduction steps, complete errors, environment details, and recent changes.

faq.question: Can it help with performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize profiling, baseline comparison, bottleneck hypotheses, controlled measurements, and verification benchmarks.

faq.question: Will it always identify the root cause?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on available evidence and reproducibility. The skill narrows uncertainty but cannot guarantee access to the responsible system state.
